title: 8 shot, including 4 children, in Coney Island, NYPD says - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
abc NEWS - At least eight people, including four children, were shot during an incident in Brooklyn's Coney Island late on the Fourth of July, the New York Police Department said.

Officers responded at about 10:37 p.m. to reports of a shooting on the 2900 block of West 31st Street, the NYPD said in a statement.

The injured, who were not publicly identified, included a 37-year-old man, a 33-year-old man, a 25-year-old woman, a 21-year-old woman, a 14-year-old boy, a 12-year-old boy, a 7-year-old boy and a 6-year-old boy.

"All victims were transported by EMS to local area hospitals where seven people were listed in stable condition," the NYPD said. "The 21-year-old woman is listed in critical condition."

Police said they recovered a firearm at the scene but have not made any arrests.

title: 16 injured in Negombo Prison clash; STF deployed to restore order - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 5 (Daily Mirror) - At least 16 inmates were injured following a clash between two groups of prisoners at the Negombo Prison, police said.

According to the Director of the Negombo Hospital, all 16 injured inmates were admitted to the hospital for treatment after the unrest inside the prison.

In response to the incident, authorities deployed the Police Special Task Force (STF) to assist in bringing the situation under control.

title: 75 drowning fatalities recorded so far this year - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 5 (Daily Mirror) - At least 75 people have lost their lives in drowning incidents during the first months of this year.

According to Police, the majority of the fatal incidents occurred when individuals entered unmonitored or hazardous locations to bathe or swim.

Police statistics also show that drowning remains a significant public safety concern, with 450 drowning-related deaths recorded across the country in 2025.

In view of the continuing fatalities, the Police has urged the public and tourists to avoid entering water at locations identified as unsafe and to exercise extreme caution when visiting rivers, reservoirs, beaches and other water bodies.

title: Missing service weapon of Yatiyantota Traffic OIC recovered from Kelani River - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 5 (Daily Mirror) - The official service firearm belonging to the Officer-in-Charge (OIC) of the Traffic Branch of the Yatiyantota Police, which had been reported missing, has been recovered from the Kelani River.

According to the police, a stock of ammunition was also retrieved from the river along with the weapon.

The Traffic OIC was arrested on June 28 on charges of failing to properly hand over his official service firearm and 10 rounds of ammunition. Following his arrest, he was produced before the Ruwanwella Magistrate's Court and subsequently remanded in custody.

title: Mahinda Rajapaksa confident Opposition can form new government - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 5 (Daily Mirror) - Former President Mahinda Rajapaksa expressed confidence that a new government could be formed if all opposition parties unite, stating that the opposition is currently in a strong position.

Speaking to the media after attending a religious ceremony, Rajapaksa said that cooperation among opposition parties would create the conditions necessary to establish a new administration.

Commenting on the current situation of opposition politicians, including those who are in custody, he said that although some leaders have been imprisoned, their political parties and remaining members continue to carry out their activities.

Responding to questions regarding recent legal action against members of his political circle and family, Rajapaksa alleged that the cases were politically motivated. He claimed that such actions were acts of political retaliation by the present government.

When asked about the return of former Minister Basil Rajapaksa to Sri Lanka, the former President said he was unaware of his schedule and that the question should be directed to Basil Rajapaksa himself.

title: National Commission on Women briefs Prime Minister on operational progress - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 5 (Daily Mirror) - The Chairperson of the Independent National Commission on Women, Ambassador Grace Asirwatham, together with the Commissioners, met with the Prime Minister to brief her on the progress made in operationalising the Commission.

During the meeting, the delegation provided an update on the implementation of the Women Empowerment Act, No. 37 of 2024, under which the National Commission on Women was established as Sri Lanka's first independent statutory body mandated to promote, protect and advance women's rights while driving the national agenda for women's empowerment.

Chairperson Ambassador Grace Asirwatham, Commissioners Jayanthi Kuru-Utumpala, Janaha Selvaras, Dr. Padma Gunaratne and M.U. Gayani, along with Executive Director K.D.R. Olga, outlined the Commission's ongoing institutional development and preparatory work to establish mechanisms across its key functions. These include advocacy, advisory, monitoring, investigative and coordination roles carried out within its statutory mandate.

The Prime Minister acknowledged the progress made and reaffirmed the Government's commitment to supporting the Commission's full operationalisation as an independent national institution dedicated to advancing women's rights, gender equality and women's empowerment in Sri Lanka.

title: Red notice fugitive in Akuregoda double murder extradited from Maldives - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 5 (Daily Mirror) - A suspect wanted in connection with the Akuregoda double murder and the subject of an International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol) Red Notice was arrested upon his arrival at Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA), Katunayake, after being extradited from the Maldives on 4 July 2026.

According to Police, the 23-year-old suspect, a resident of Ethulgama, was brought back to Sri Lanka by a team of officers from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID). He was identified and detained at the airport through the automated biometric E-gate system before being handed over to the Western Province South Crime Division for further investigations.

Investigators allege that the suspect played a key role in the double murder that occurred on 13 February 2026 in the Akuregoda area under the Thalangama Police Division. The victims, an attorney-at-law and his wife, were shot while travelling in their vehicle. Police believe the suspect drove the getaway vehicle used by the gunmen following the attack.

Police further stated that the suspect has a criminal history and was out on strict bail over previous cases at the time of the double murder. He had been arrested by the Malwathuhiripitiya Police on 21 October 2025 for the unlawful possession of a T-56 assault rifle and later released on strict bail by the Minuwangoda Magistrate's Court. He was also arrested by the Welikada Police on 15 December 2025 for heroin possession and subsequently released on strict bail by the relevant Magistrate's Court.

The Western Province South Crime Division is continuing investigations to determine the suspect's alleged links to the organized criminal network believed to be behind the Akuregoda double murder.
